terms.explanation: Starts quickly and does not last long.
From the Latin 'bis in die'.

terms.plain: Main problem that brought you in

terms.explanation: Lasts for months or years.
The name of the illness.
What has happened in the past.
No food or drink, including water.
terms.aliases: nil per os, fasting, nothing to eat or drink

terms.explanation: Take the medicine only if you have the symptom.

terms.plain: What is likely to happen over time
Illness is not active right now

terms.explanation: Do it immediately.
What the patient says is wrong.

terms.plain: Body reacting to something it is allergic to
terms.explanation: It can cause itching, rash, swelling, or trouble breathing.
A sudden, serious allergic reaction that can make it hard to breathe. It is an emergency.
Not enough healthy red blood cells to carry oxygen. It can cause tiredness and pale skin.

terms.plain: Chest pain from the heart not getting enough blood
terms.explanation: Pain or pressure that often comes with effort and eases with rest.

terms.plain: Strong worry or fear that does not go away

terms.explanation: Pain that often starts near the belly button and moves to the lower right side.
The airways in the lungs get narrow and swollen, causing wheezing, cough, and trouble breathing.
The upper chambers of the heart beat in an uneven, often fast way. It raises the risk of stroke.
A growth that does not spread to other parts of the body.
The tubes that carry air to the lungs are swollen and make mucus, causing a cough.
The skin becomes red, warm, swollen, and painful.
Blood flow to part of the brain is blocked, or a blood vessel in the brain bursts.
The kidneys slowly lose their ability to clean the blood.

terms.plain: Long-term lung disease that makes breathing hard
terms.explanation: A group of lung diseases, often caused by smoking, that make it hard to breathe out. It includes emphysema and chronic bronchitis.
Long-term liver damage that makes the liver work poorly.

terms.plain: Brain injury from a hit to the head
terms.explanation: It can cause headache, confusion, dizziness, or memory problems.
The heart does not pump blood as well as it should, so fluid can build up in the lungs and legs.

terms.plain: Blood clot in a leg vein
terms.explanation: A clot in a deep vein, usually in the leg. It can cause pain and swelling.

terms.plain: Not enough water in the body
terms.explanation: It can cause thirst, dark urine, dizziness, and tiredness.

terms.plain: Memory and thinking loss that gets worse over time

terms.explanation: Feeling very sad or empty for weeks or longer, or losing interest in things.
The body cannot control blood sugar properly because it makes too little insulin or cannot use it well.
Infection of the stomach and bowel causing vomiting and diarrhea.
Stomach acid keeps coming back up into the food pipe.
High blood sugar that first shows up during pregnancy.
Often caused by a virus, alcohol, or medicine.
Too much sugar in the blood. It can cause thirst, peeing a lot, and tiredness.
Too much fat in the blood, which can raise the risk of heart disease.
Blood pushes too hard against the walls of your blood vessels. It can raise the risk of heart attack and stroke.
The thyroid gland makes too much hormone, which can cause weight loss, fast heartbeat, and sweating.
Blood sugar has dropped too low. It can cause shakiness, sweating, confusion, or passing out.
Blood pressure that is lower than normal. It can cause dizziness or fainting.
The thyroid gland makes too little hormone, which can cause tiredness, weight gain, and feeling cold.
Cancer cells that can grow and spread to other parts of the body.
Cancer that has moved from where it started to another part of the body.
Often one-sided and may come with nausea or sensitivity to light.
Blood flow to part of the heart is blocked and the heart muscle starts to get damaged.
A lump of cells that grow in an abnormal way. It may or may not be cancer.
The cushioning in joints wears down over time, causing pain and stiffness.
Bones become fragile and break more easily.
An infection that fills parts of the lungs with fluid or pus.
A serious pregnancy problem with high blood pressure and protein in the urine.
A clot that travels to the lungs and blocks blood flow. It is an emergency.

terms.plain: Arthritis caused by the immune system
terms.explanation: The body's defense system attacks the joints, causing pain and swelling.
A sudden burst of electrical activity in the brain that can cause shaking, staring, or passing out.
The body's response to an infection starts to harm its own organs. It is an emergency.
Stroke-like symptoms that go away within minutes to hours but warn that a full stroke could happen.

terms.plain: Cold or throat and nose infection

terms.explanation: A germ infection in the bladder or urine passages that can cause burning when you pee.
Sold in Canada as Tylenol. Too much can damage the liver.
It does not work on colds or flu, which are caused by viruses.
Helps stop blood clots from forming. It can cause bleeding.
Used for asthma and COPD.

terms.plain: Not safe for you to use
terms.explanation: A medicine or treatment that should not be used because it could cause harm.
Helps the body get rid of extra water by making you pee more.

terms.plain: Hormone given by injection to lower blood sugar
terms.explanation: Too much can cause low blood sugar.
Examples include ibuprofen. It can upset the stomach and affect the kidneys.
Examples include morphine. It can cause drowsiness and slow breathing, and can be addictive.

terms.plain: Medicine you can buy without a prescription
Medicine that makes you calm or sleepy

terms.explanation: You are moved from the emergency room into a hospital bed.

terms.plain: Chest pushes and breaths to restart the heart
Thin tube placed in the body
terms.explanation: For example, a tube to drain urine from the bladder.

terms.plain: Machine that cleans your blood when kidneys cannot

terms.explanation: You are well enough to go home, often with instructions.

terms.plain: Do not try to restart my heart or breathing
terms.explanation: A medical order that says CPR should not be done.

terms.plain: A return visit to check how you are doing
Medicine that puts you fully to sleep for surgery
Your agreement after being told the risks and benefits
terms.explanation: You have the right to ask questions and say no.
Medicine or fluid goes straight into a vein through a small tube.

terms.plain: Breathing tube placed in the windpipe
terms.explanation: A tube helps you breathe, usually with a machine.

terms.plain: Numbing medicine for one small area
Care focused on comfort during serious illness
terms.explanation: It aims to ease pain and stress. It can be given alongside other treatment.
Your doctor asks another doctor or service to see you.
Used to close a cut or surgery wound.

terms.plain: Sorting patients by how urgent their problem is
terms.explanation: The sickest patients are seen first, not always in the order they arrived.
Not feeling like eating. This is different from the eating disorder anorexia nervosa.

terms.plain: Pain or pressure in the chest
terms.explanation: Pain, tightness, or squeezing in the chest.
Fewer bowel movements than usual, or stools that are hard and painful to pass.

terms.plain: Blue or gray skin, lips, or nails
terms.explanation: Skin turning bluish because of low oxygen.
Sweating a lot, often without heat or exercise.
Going to the toilet more often than usual with loose or watery stool.
Food or drink feels stuck or is hard to swallow.
Trouble making normal voice sounds.
Feeling short of breath or like you cannot get enough air.

terms.plain: Pain or burning when you pee

terms.explanation: Extra fluid building up in the body, often in the legs, ankles, or feet.
Food or liquid coming back up through the mouth.
Tiredness that does not go away with rest.
Blood in your vomit. It can look red or like coffee grounds.
Pee that looks pink, red, or brown.
A general feeling of being sick or run down.
Dark black stool with a very bad smell. It can mean bleeding in the stomach or gut.
The feeling that you might throw up.

terms.plain: Feeling your heart race, pound, or skip
terms.explanation: Noticing that your heartbeat is fast, strong, or uneven.
Tingling, prickling, or numb feeling, often in the hands or feet.
Passing much more urine than usual.
Body temperature higher than normal.
Briefly passing out and then waking up again.
Feeling that you or the room is spinning.

terms.plain: Small sample of tissue taken for testing
terms.explanation: A tiny piece of tissue is taken and looked at under a microscope.
Measures the amount of sugar in your blood.

terms.plain: Pressure of blood in your blood vessels
terms.explanation: Shown as two numbers, like 120/80. The top number is when the heart pumps. The bottom is when it rests.
A number that compares your weight with your height.

terms.plain: Camera test of the large bowel
terms.explanation: A thin tube with a camera looks inside the large bowel.
Counts red cells, white cells, and platelets to check for anemia, infection, and other problems.
You lie on a table that slides through a large ring. It takes detailed pictures of the inside of the body.
A waste product in the blood that shows how well the kidneys work.

terms.plain: Test to find the germ and the right antibiotic
terms.explanation: A sample is grown in a lab to see which germ is causing the infection and which medicine works.
Sticky patches on the chest record the electrical activity of the heart.
Checks salts like sodium and potassium that your body needs to work well.

terms.plain: Camera test of the throat and stomach
terms.explanation: A thin tube with a camera goes down the throat to look inside.
A home test used to screen for bowel cancer.
Shows your average blood sugar over about the last 3 months.
Shows how long your blood takes to clot. It is used to check some blood thinners.
Measures cholesterol and fats in the blood.
A loud machine takes detailed pictures without radiation. Metal in or on the body can be unsafe.
A low-dose X-ray used to look for breast cancer.
A few cells are taken from the cervix to check for changes that could lead to cancer.
A blood test that can be higher when there is a problem with the prostate.
A small clip on the finger shows how much oxygen is in your blood.
You blow into a tube to measure how well your lungs work.
A protein that goes up in the blood when the heart muscle is damaged.
A small handheld device on the skin shows pictures of the inside of the body.
Checks your urine for infection, blood, sugar, and other signs of illness.
Temperature, pulse, breathing rate, blood pressure, and oxygen level.
A quick picture that uses a small amount of radiation.
Millimetres of mercury.

terms.plain: Unit for blood sugar and blood tests in Canada
terms.explanation: Millimoles per litre. Canadian labs report blood sugar in this unit.

history_questions.plain_question: What is the main problem that brought you here today?
When did it begin? Was it sudden or slow?
Where do you feel it? Please point with one finger.

history_questions.clinical_phrase: How long does it last? Is it constant or intermittent?
history_questions.plain_question: How long does it last? Is it there all the time, or does it come and go?
From 0 (no pain) to 10 (worst pain you can imagine), how bad is it?

history_questions.clinical_phrase: Describe the quality of the pain.
history_questions.plain_question: What does it feel like? Sharp, dull, burning, squeezing, or something else?
Does the pain move anywhere else in your body?
Do you have anything else with it, such as fever, throwing up, or trouble breathing?

history_questions.clinical_phrase: Any chest pain, dyspnea, syncope, or unilateral weakness?
history_questions.plain_question: Have you had chest pain, trouble breathing, fainting, or weakness on one side of your body?

history_questions.clinical_phrase: Do you have any drug allergies? What is the reaction?
history_questions.plain_question: Are you allergic to any medicine, food, or anything else? What happens when you react?

history_questions.clinical_phrase: List current medications including OTC and supplements.
history_questions.plain_question: What medicines do you take? Please include vitamins, herbal products, and anything you buy without a prescription.
Have you had any serious illness, surgery, or hospital stays?
Has anyone in your family had heart disease, diabetes, cancer, or stroke?

history_questions.clinical_phrase: Is there a possibility of pregnancy?
Tobacco, alcohol, and recreational drug use?
history_questions.plain_question: Do you smoke, drink alcohol, or use any drugs?
